5.title: The Sermon on the Mount Begins
5.text: Christ went up into a mountain, and his disciples came to him. He begins not with rebukes but with blessings — eight beatitudes that overturn the world's reckoning. Blessed are the poor in spirit, the mourners, the meek, the hungry for righteousness, the merciful, the pure in heart, the peacemakers, and the persecuted. The disciples are then named salt and light, that men may see their good works and glorify their Father. Christ has not come to destroy the law but to fulfill it; he then deepens its demands — anger is murder of the heart, lust is adultery, and love must extend even to enemies. Be ye therefore perfect, as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.

6.title: Spiritual Disciplines and Trust
6.text: Three spiritual disciplines — almsgiving, prayer, fasting — are to be done before God, not for the praise of men. Christ teaches the disciples to pray: hallowed be thy name, thy kingdom come, thy will be done. Lay not up treasures on earth, but in heaven; where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. No man can serve two masters; therefore take no anxious thought for tomorrow. Behold the fowls of the air and the lilies of the field — your heavenly Father knows what you need. Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you.

28.title: Resurrection and the Great Commission
28.text: On the first day of the week, the women find the tomb empty and an angel's word: 'He is not here, for he is risen, as he said.' Christ meets them, then meets the eleven on the appointed mountain in Galilee. There he claims all authority in heaven and on earth, and commissions his disciples: 'Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost; teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you.' His parting word is also his abiding promise: 'Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.'
